derivation: Normal: each unstable entry targets a stable one. Stable outputs: column 0 has 1,3 with z=0; column 1 has 2,4 with z=1. No pair is stable in a common column with different z, so no pair is output-incompatible.
No incompatibility can be implied, so {1,2,3,4} is compatible. Its class set is empty (N(C,0)={1,3} and N(C,1)={2,4} are both inside C), so it dominates every proper subset: it is the only prime.

Cover {1,2,3,4} is closed. Reduced: column 0 is stable with z=0 (from 1 and 3), column 1 is stable with z=1 (from 2 and 4): a one-state machine where z follows x. The four-state original only counted parity, which is unobservable.
